## TypeScript Best Practices

- Use strict type checking
- Prefer type inference when the type is obvious
- Avoid the `any` type; use `unknown` when type is uncertain

- Always use angular schematics for new files (ng generate ...) unless there is no generator

  - For pages use `ng g c ... --type=page`
  - For models use `ng g interface ...`

- Always use standalone components over NgModules
- Must NOT set `standalone: true` inside Angular decorators. It's the default in Angular v20+.
- Do NOT set `changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush` explicitly. `OnPush` is the default in Angular v22+.
- Use signals for state management
- Implement lazy loading for feature routes
- Do NOT use the `@HostBinding` and `@HostListener` decorators. Put host bindings inside the `host` object of the `@Component` or `@Directive` decorator instead
- Use `NgOptimizedImage` for all static images.
  - `NgOptimizedImage` does not work for inline base64 images.

## Accessibility Requirements

- It MUST pass all AXE checks.
- It MUST follow all WCAG AA minimums, including focus management, color contrast, and ARIA attributes.

## Components

- Keep components small and focused on a single responsibility
- Use `input()` and `output()` functions instead of decorators
- Use `model()` for two-way bound properties with `[(prop)]` syntax instead of pairing `input()` with `output()`
- Use `computed()` for derived state
- Use `linkedSignal()` for state derived from multiple reactive sources that must stay synchronized

import express from 'express';
import cors from 'cors';
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join, dirname } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import YAML from 'yaml';
import swaggerUi from 'swagger-ui-express';

import authRoutes from './routes/auth.js';
import contactsRoutes from './routes/contacts.js';
import dealsRoutes from './routes/deals.js';
import tasksRoutes from './routes/tasks.js';
import { errorHandler } from './middleware/error.js';

const __filename = fileURLToPath(import.meta.url);
const __dirname = dirname(__filename);

const app = express();
const PORT = process.env['PORT'] ?? 3000;

// ─── Global middleware ────────────────────────────────
app.use(cors());
app.use(express.json());

// ─── OpenAPI / Swagger UI ─────────────────────────────
const openapiPath = join(__dirname, '..', 'openapi.yaml');
const openapiDoc = YAML.parse(readFileSync(openapiPath, 'utf-8'));
app.use('/api-docs', swaggerUi.serve, swaggerUi.setup(openapiDoc));

// ─── API routes ───────────────────────────────────────
app.use('/api/auth', authRoutes);
app.use('/api/contacts', contactsRoutes);
app.use('/api/deals', dealsRoutes);
app.use('/api/deals/:dealId/tasks', tasksRoutes);

// ─── Error handler (must be last) ─────────────────────
app.use(errorHandler as any);

// ─── Start ────────────────────────────────────────────
app.listen(PORT, () => {
  console.log(`🚀 CRM API server running at http://localhost:${PORT}/api`);
  console.log(`📖 Swagger UI at http://localhost:${PORT}/api-docs`);
});
```
</details></tool-use>

import type { Request, Response, NextFunction } from 'express';

/**
 * Mock auth middleware.
 * Validates that the Authorization header contains a Bearer token
 * with the prefix `mock-access-`. Attaches `userId` to the request.
 */
export function authMiddleware(req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction): void {
  const header = req.headers.authorization;

  if (!header?.startsWith('Bearer ')) {
    res.status(401).json({
      error: { status: 401, message: 'Missing or invalid authorization header', code: 'UNAUTHORIZED' },
    });
    return;
  }

  const token = header.slice(7);

  if (!token.startsWith('mock-access-')) {
    res.status(403).json({
      error: { status: 403, message: 'Invalid access token', code: 'UNAUTHORIZED' },
    });
    return;
  }

  // Attach the user id extracted from the mock token
  (req as any).userId = token.replace('mock-access-', '');
  next();
}
```
</details></tool-use>

import { inject, Service } from '@angular/core';
import { Deal } from '@feature/deals/model/deal';

// const API_URL = `http://localhost:3000/api/`;

import { HttpClient } from '@angular/common/http';
import { map, Observable } from 'rxjs';

type PagingObject<T> = { items: T[]; limit: number; offset: number };

@Service()
export class DealsAPI {
  http = inject(HttpClient);

  fetchDeals(q = '') {
    return this.http
      .get<PagingObject<Deal>>(`deals`, {
        params: { q: q },
      })
      .pipe(map((res) => res.items));
  }

  fetchDealById(id = '') {
    return this.http.get<Deal>(`deals/${id}`, {});
  }
}
```

## Plan: Minimal login/logout + bearer/refresh + AuthInterceptor

Decisions: tokens in localStorage; dedicated /login page; auth guard on /deals; server keeps accepting any credentials.

Steps
1. Auth service (src/app/core/auth/auth.ts): signal session {accessToken, refreshToken}, hydrate from localStorage; login(email,[REDACTED:generic-password]) -> POST auth/login; logout() clears storage and navigates /login; refreshToken() -> POST auth/refresh with stored refreshToken, tap() saves new pair, emits; on failure logout. getHeaders() uses current accessToken.
2. HttpContext flag SKIP_AUTH (core/http/index.ts): set on login/refresh requests so AuthInterceptor does not attach Bearer and does not recurse on 403.
3. AuthInterceptor (core/http/index.ts): keep defer + retry(count 1) on 403 -> refresh; 401 -> logout + /login. Ensure refresh errors resolve to logout (not raw error).
4. Login page (ng g c ... --type=page under core/auth): email/[REDACTED:generic-password] form, calls Auth.login, navigates to /deals; shows server error.
5. Guard (src/app/core/auth/auth.guard.ts, new): CanActivateFn returning UrlTree to /login when not logged in.
6. Routes (src/app/app.routes.ts): add lazy 'login' route; add canActivate authGuard to 'deals'.
7. Toolbar (src/app/app.ts): Login button -> routerLink /login, shown when logged out; Logout button -> auth.logout(), shown when logged in (@if on signal).

Relevant files
- src/app/core/auth/auth.ts (rewrite stub: hardcoded token, refreshToken returns of(true))
- src/app/core/http/index.ts (AuthInterceptor, add SKIP_AUTH context)
- src/app/app.config.ts (no change; interceptor order URL -> Error -> Auth)
- src/app/app.routes.ts, src/app/app.ts
- server/src/routes/auth.ts (no change; login/refresh/me exist, mock tokens mock-access-u1 / mock-refresh-u1)
- server/src/middleware/auth.ts (401 missing header, 403 invalid token)

Verification
1. ng build passes; npm run lint/test if configured.
2. Start server + ng serve. Login -> redirected to /deals, requests carry Bearer.
3. Set invalid token in localStorage -> request gets 403 -> refresh -> retry succeeds.
4. Invalid refresh token -> 401 -> logout, redirect to /login.
5. Logout -> /deals redirects to /login; reload keeps session only while logged in.

Scope excluded: server-side token expiry/validation, proactive refresh timer, returnUrl, Settings button, role/permissions, server logout endpoint (none in openapi).

Open notes: server tokens never expire; refresh only triggers on 403. Interceptor 401 path returns EMPTY (observables never emit) - acceptable for minimal scope.

## Plan: Minimal login/logout, bearer token, refresh, and AuthInterceptor

Tokens go in `localStorage`, login is a dedicated `/login` page, and `/deals` is protected by a guard. The mock server keeps accepting any credentials. Current state:  in `src/app/core/auth/auth.ts` has a hardcoded token and a stub , and the `src/app/core/http/index.ts#L40` already retries once on 403 and redirects on 401. The server already provides `POST /api/auth/login`, `POST /api/auth/refresh`, and `GET /api/auth/me`.

**Steps**
1. **Auth service** (`src/app/core/auth/auth.ts`): hold `{accessToken, refreshToken}` in a signal, hydrated from `localStorage`. Add `login(email, [REDACTED:generic-password])`, `logout()` (clears storage, navigates to `/login`), and make  call `auth/refresh`, save the new pair with `tap`, and log out on failure.  reads the current access token.
2. **Skip flag** (http/index.ts): add an `HttpContextToken` such as `SKIP_AUTH`, set on login and refresh requests, so the interceptor does not attach a Bearer header and cannot recurse on 403. *Depends on 1.*
3. **AuthInterceptor** (`src/app/core/http/index.ts#L40`): keep `defer` (headers rebuilt per attempt) and `retry({count: 1})` on 403. Make refresh failure end in logout rather than a raw error. *Depends on 1 and 2.*
4. **Login page** (generate with `ng g c ... --type=page` under `core/auth`): email and [REDACTED:generic-password] form, calls , navigates to `/deals` on success, shows the server error on failure. *Depends on 1.*
5. **Guard** (new `core/auth/auth.guard.ts`): `CanActivateFn` returning a `UrlTree` to `/login` when not logged in. *Depends on 1.*
6. **Routes** (`src/app/app.routes.ts`): add a lazy `login` route and `canActivate: [authGuard]` on `deals`. *Depends on 4 and 5.*
7. **Toolbar** (`src/app/app.ts#L18-L19`): Login button uses `routerLink="/login"` and shows when logged out. Logout button calls  and shows when logged in, via `@if` on the signal. *Depends on 1.*

Steps 2, 4, and 5 can run in parallel once step 1 is done.

**Relevant files**
- `auth.ts`: replace the stub with session state, `login`, `logout`, and real .
- `index.ts`:  changes and the new `SKIP_AUTH` context.
- `app.config.ts`: no change needed; interceptor order is URL → Error → Auth.
- `app.routes.ts`: login route and guard.
- `app.ts`: Login/Logout buttons.
- `auth.ts`: no change. Mock tokens are `mock-access-u1` and `mock-refresh-u1`.
- `auth.ts`: 401 for a missing header, 403 for an invalid token.

**Verification**
1. `ng build` passes, and the existing `npm test` task runs.
2. Start the server and `ng serve`. Log in, get redirected to `/deals`, and confirm requests carry `Authorization: Bearer mock-access-u1`.
3. Set an invalid access token in `localStorage`. The next request should get 403, refresh, and succeed on retry.
4. Set an invalid refresh token and force a 403. Expect a 401 from refresh, logout, and a redirect to `/login`.
5. Log out, then open `/deals`. Expect a redirect to `/login`. After reload, the session should persist only while logged in.

**Decisions**
- Tokens in `localStorage`. Survives reload.
- Dedicated `/login` route, not a dialog.
- Guard applied to `/deals`.
- Server login behaviour unchanged, so any credentials are accepted. Note that  has `admin@example.com` / , which is unused.

**Excluded from scope**
- Server-side token expiry or validation.
- Proactive refresh timer. Refresh only happens on 403.
- `returnUrl` after login.
- The Settings button.
- Roles and permissions.
- A server logout endpoint. None exists in `openapi.yaml`, so logout is client-only.

**Further considerations**
1. Refresh-token rotation: the server returns a new pair from `/auth/refresh`, so store both. Recommended.
2. The 401 path in  returns `EMPTY`, so pending subscribers never emit. Acceptable for a minimal scope; changing it to an error would be a small follow-up.
3. Before implementing, confirm whether `@angular/forms/signals` (Signal Forms, as the Angular rules recommend) is available in `package.json`. Otherwise Reactive forms will be used.

The plan is saved at `/memories/session/plan.md`. Let me know if you want changes, or say "approve" to proceed with implementation.

HttpClient, HttpContext, HttpContextToken } from '@angular/common/http';
import { computed, inject, Service, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { Router } from '@angular/router';
import { Observable, tap } from 'rxjs';
import { AuthTokens } from './auth-tokens';

export const SKIP_AUTH = new HttpContextToken(() => false);

const STORAGE_KEY = 'auth.tokens';

@Service()
export class Auth {
  private readonly http = inject(HttpClient);
  private readonly router = inject(Router);
  private readonly tokens = signal<AuthTokens | null>(this.readStoredTokens());

  readonly isLoggedIn = computed(() => this.tokens() !== null);

  public getHeaders(): Record<string, string> {
    const accessToken = this.tokens()?.accessToken;
    return accessToken ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}` } : {};
  }

  public login(email: string, [REDACTED:generic-password]: string): Observable<AuthTokens> {
    return this.http
      .post<AuthTokens>('auth/login', { email, [REDACTED:generic-password] }, { context: new HttpContext().set(SKIP_AUTH, true) })
      .pipe(tap((tokens) => this.setTokens(tokens)));
  }

  public refreshToken(): Observable<AuthTokens> {
    const refreshToken = this.tokens()?.refreshToken ?? '';
    return this.http
      .post<AuthTokens>('auth/refresh', { refreshToken }, { context: new HttpContext().set(SKIP_AUTH, true) })
      .pipe(tap((tokens) => this.setTokens(tokens)));
  }

  public logout() {
    this.setTokens(null);
    this.router.navigateByUrl('/login');
  }

  private setTokens(tokens: AuthTokens | null) {
    this.tokens.set(tokens);
    if (tokens) localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, JSON.stringify(tokens));
    else localStorage.removeItem(STORAGE_KEY);
  }

  private readStoredTokens(): AuthTokens | null {
    const stored = localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY);
    return stored ? (JSON.parse(stored) as AuthTokens) : null;
```

, inject, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { email, form, FormField, required, submit } from '@angular/forms/signals';
import { Router } from '@angular/router';
import { Auth } from '@core/auth/auth';
import { lastValueFrom } from 'rxjs';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-login',
  imports: [FormField],
  template: `
    <form class="mx-auto flex max-w-sm flex-col gap-4 p-6" novalidate (submit)="onSubmit($event)">
      <h1 class="text-2xl font-semibold">Login</h1>

      <label class="flex flex-col gap-1">
        Email
        <input
          type="email"
          autocomplete="username"
          class="rounded border px-3 py-2"
          [formField]="loginForm.email"
          [attr.aria-invalid]="loginForm.email().touched() && loginForm.email().invalid()"
        />
      </label>
      @if (loginForm.email().touched() && loginForm.email().invalid()) {
        <p role="alert" class="text-sm text-red-600">Enter a valid email address.</p>
      }

      <label class="flex flex-col gap-1">
        Password
        <input
          type="[REDACTED:generic-password]"
          autocomplete="current-[REDACTED:generic-password]"
          class="rounded border px-3 py-2"
          [formField]="loginForm.[REDACTED:generic-password]"
          [attr.aria-invalid]="loginForm.[REDACTED:generic-password]().touched() && loginForm.[REDACTED:generic-password]().invalid()"
        />
      </label>
      @if (loginForm.[REDACTED:generic-password]().touched() && loginForm.[REDACTED:generic-password]().invalid()) {
        <p role="alert" class="text-sm text-red-600">Password is required.</p>
      }

      @if (serverError()) {
        <p role="alert" class="text-sm text-red-600">{{ serverError() }}</p>
      }

      <button type="submit" class="rounded bg-blue-600 px-4 py-2 text-white">Login</button>
    </form>
  `,
})
export class LoginPage {
  private readonly auth = inject(Auth);
  private readonly router = inject(Router);

  private readonly credentials = signal({ email: '', [REDACTED:generic-password]: '' });
  readonly loginForm = form(this.credentials, (path) => {
    required(path.email);
    email(path.email);
    required(path.[REDACTED:generic-password]);
  });
  readonly serverError = signal<string | null>(null);

  onSubmit(event: Event) {
    event.preventDefault();

    void submit(this.loginForm, async () => {

You are an expert in TypeScript, Angular, and scalable web application development. You write functional, maintainable, performant, and accessible code following Angular and TypeScript best practices.

## TypeScript Best Practices

- Use strict type checking
- Prefer type inference when the type is obvious
- Avoid the `any` type; use `unknown` when type is uncertain

## Angular Best Practices

- Always use angular schematics for new files (ng generate ...) unless there is no generator
  - Do not change options - schematic will use angular.json defaults
  - For pages use `ng g c ... --type=page`
  - For models use `ng g interface ...`
  - For data sources and services use `ng g s ...`

- Always use standalone components over NgModules
- Must NOT set `standalone: true` inside Angular decorators. It's the default in Angular v20+.
- Do NOT set `changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush` explicitly. `OnPush` is the default in Angular v22+.
- Use signals for state management
- Implement lazy loading for feature routes
- Do NOT use the `@HostBinding` and `@HostListener` decorators. Put host bindings inside the `host` object of the `@Component` or `@Directive` decorator instead
- Use `NgOptimizedImage` for all static images.
  - `NgOptimizedImage` does not work for inline base64 images.

## Accessibility Requirements

- It MUST pass all AXE checks.
